descriptor.name: Security Patch and Build Timestamp Coherence
descriptor.description: Compares each partition's declared Android security-patch level against the compile timestamp of that same partition, because a stock image declares a patch at most a few weeks after it was built. The comparison stays inside the property set and therefore survives a forged key attestation.

evidenceUnits.title: Declared patch level versus own build timestamp
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Per-partition pairs of security-patch level and build timestamp properties, such as ro.build.version.security_patch with ro.build.date.utc
evidenceUnits.proposition: A partition declares a security-patch level dated substantially later than the compile timestamp of that same partition, which no genuine build can produce
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Bionic system property reads through __system_property_get
evidenceUnits.availability: Available when at least one partition publishes both a YYYY-MM-DD patch level and an epoch build timestamp; partitions publishing only one half are reported as not comparable
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Both values are read from the same property set, so this compares two values an attacker could control; it holds only because spoofing tools rewrite the patch level while leaving build timestamps intact
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Proves the patch level was set after the image was produced but does not name the tool that set it; stock images legitimately declare a patch up to about two months after their build, so only skew far beyond that is graded, and an attacker who also rewrites build timestamps defeats the check entirely

descriptor.name: DRM Credential and Boot State Coherence
descriptor.description: Compares the boot state the device claims through its own properties against its Widevine credential. L1 key material is erased when a bootloader is unlocked and cannot be re-provisioned from userspace, so a device claiming a locked, verified boot state while advertising L1 with no provisioned credential is stating two things that cannot both be true.

evidenceUnits.title: Claimed boot state versus Widevine credential
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Widevine plugin securityLevel and systemId read through MediaDrm, and a session open attempt, compared against ro.boot.verifiedbootstate, ro.boot.flash.locked and ro.boot.vbmeta.device_state
evidenceUnits.proposition: A device claiming a locked and verified boot state advertises Widevine L1 while its plugin reports the unprovisioned-system-ID placeholder, which a genuinely locked device would not do
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: android.media.MediaDrm for the Widevine UUID via a JNI collector, and Bionic system property reads for the claimed boot state
evidenceUnits.availability: Comparable only when Widevine is supported, the plugin advertises L1, and the boot properties claim a locked verified state; devices advertising only L3 or honestly reporting an unlocked bootloader are reported as not comparable
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Crosses from values a userspace module can rewrite to key material held by the DRM trustlet, which a module can neither forge nor re-provision, so the comparison survives property spoofing and a forged attestation keybox
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Proves the two statements are inconsistent, not which one is false or which tool caused it: an erased DRM credential can also follow a mainboard replacement or a device that never carried L1 provisioning, and no locked unmodified device has been measured, so the rate at which legitimate devices present this way is unknown

descriptor.name: Keystore Grant Chain Consistency
descriptor.description: Reads one Keystore key's attestation certificate chain twice, once by alias and once through a grant the application issues to its own uid, and compares them; a grant read-back that denies the key exists is graded separately, after a non-attested control key shows the grant path works. A stored chain is identical to every reader, so a difference proves the chain is being produced per lookup rather than returned from storage.

evidenceUnits.title: Alias-path and grant-path certificate chains
evidenceUnits.observedObject: The certificate chain of a freshly generated attested EC key, read through KeyStore.getCertificateChain and through KeyStoreManager.getGrantedCertificateChainFromId for the same key
evidenceUnits.proposition: The two readings of one key's certificate chain disagree in length or in a certificate digest, or the grant path denies that the key exists while a non-attested control key reads back through its grant, none of which storage can produce
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: AndroidKeyStore provider and the public android.security.keystore.KeyStoreManager grant API through a JNI collector
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires API 36 or later, where KeyStoreManager first ships; below that the check reports unavailable rather than clean, and attestation key generation must succeed
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Self-referential and carries no reference data, so it holds against an attestation chain that verifies to a genuine root: an interception layer must answer both lookup paths identically to stay consistent
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Proves the chain is synthesised per lookup, not which layer synthesises it or whether the attestation content is false; a layer that answers both paths identically is invisible to this check, and an isolated-process reader, which would be a stronger second path, cannot reach the Keystore service on any device

descriptor.name: SELinux Global Enforcement
descriptor.description: Cross-checks global SELinux enforcement observations, infers enforcement from a refused read of the DAC-readable enforce node, and probes enforce-node permissions without writing.

evidenceUnits.title: SELinux enforcement state
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Enforcement state reported by available SELinux sources, or inferred from an EACCES refusal to read the enforce node
evidenceUnits.proposition: One or more available sources report the current SELinux enforcement mode
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: selinuxfs and libselinux read-only queries, plus stat() of the enforce node when its read is refused with EACCES
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on selinuxfs visibility and library availability; the read-denial inference needs selinuxfs confirmed by statfs and a DAC mode that permits the read, measured by stat() or taken from the kernel constant 0644 when stat() is refused

descriptor.name: System Property Source Integrity
descriptor.description: Cross-checks equivalent Android property sources and parses property areas with explicit failure states.

evidenceUnits.title: Equivalent property-source consistency
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Equivalent Android property values read through multiple sources
evidenceUnits.proposition: Available sources either agree or satisfy an explicit mismatch rule for the same property
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Comparison across the bionic callback accessor, the bionic legacy accessor, android.os.SystemProperties, a forked getprop, the parsed property-area bytes, android.os.Build, and /proc/cmdline boot parameters
evidenceUnits.availability: A comparison is possible only when enough equivalent sources return usable values
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: All user-space sources can share mediation; agreement is not proof of kernel-level integrity. Only /proc/cmdline sits below user space, and only the property-area source bypasses the bionic accessor
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Strength is graded by which source is the outlier rather than by how many sources disagree: a kernel-versus-userspace or property-area-versus-accessor contradiction is STRONG, a Java-API or separate-process outlier is MODERATE, and an android.os.Build outlier is WEAK because the property may simply have changed after process start. Values are trimmed, lowercased and boolean-aliased before comparison, so a case-only or formatting-only spoof is not detected. Missing or failed sources remain collection state rather than negative evidence

evidenceUnits.title: Property-area allocation integrity
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Parsed property-area allocation and unreferenced byte ranges
evidenceUnits.proposition: Visible property areas exhibit structural Trie integrity without orphaned unreferenced allocations
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Direct read-only parsing of visible property-area files
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on path visibility, permissions, and compatible property-area format
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The app-visible files and parser remain below the kernel or privileged service trust boundary
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Unreferenced allocation indicates modified or deleted Trie nodes (e.g. via resetprop), though atypical OEM layouts remain possible

descriptor.name: Cross-Process Descriptor Forensics
descriptor.description: Cross-checks three independent kernel views of the process descriptor table in the host process and in a helper process forked fresh from Zygote, and carries a cross-process trap descriptor as telemetry.

evidenceUnits.title: Descriptor table view differential
evidenceUnits.observedObject: The open file descriptors of the host process and of a dedicated helper process, as reported by three independent kernel interfaces
evidenceUnits.proposition: The descriptor table, the /proc/self/fd lookup path and the /proc/self/fd iteration path disagree about the same descriptor across repeated sweeps
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: fcntl(F_GETFD) against readlink(/proc/self/fd/<n>) against readdir(/proc/self/fd), repeated in the host process and in an android:process helper
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires a readable /proc/self/fd; the comparison is skipped when procfs resolves no descriptors at all
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: A kernel-resident hook that filters both the lookup and the iteration path consistently would defeat the comparison, as would one that also intercepts fcntl
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A stable disagreement is a contradiction in the kernel's own descriptor accounting and needs no device threshold, but it identifies procfs filtering in general rather than any specific tool. Reported at MODERATE while the detector is EXPERIMENTAL because no clean-device baseline exists for the residual race rate.

evidenceUnits.title: Cross-process trap descriptor
evidenceUnits.observedObject: An unlinked, app-private trap descriptor transferred to the helper process over Binder
evidenceUnits.proposition: The trap descriptor did not survive transfer to a separately specialized process intact
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: ParcelFileDescriptor transfer, then fstat, pread of the signature payload and readlink of /proc/self/fd in the receiving process
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires the helper process to bind and the host cache directory to be writable
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The descriptor is app-private and unlinked, so only a process already holding it could alter it
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Telemetry only; this channel can never move the detector outcome. The descriptor is installed into the helper process by the binder driver after that process has finished specializing, so Zygisk-style specialization-time descriptor sanitization cannot reach it and no result here supports a tamper claim.
